name: Arevon Energy, Inc.
decision: Preserve the verified institutional ownership names. Park precise investor-vehicle and fund assignments; the evidence does not support the proposed ADIA Direct Infrastructure or APG Direct Infrastructure Pool labels.

decision_primary.quotation: Arevon Energy, Inc. is owned by three investors: APG, CalSTRS, and a wholly owned subsidiary of ADIA.
decision_primary.pdf_page_footnote: PDF page 34, printed page 34; GRI 2-1. Publication-date inconsistency appears under GRI 2-3.

preserved_ownership_facts: The company itself identifies APG, CalSTRS and an unnamed wholly owned ADIA subsidiary as its three investors.

Capital Dynamics' August 17, 2021 formation announcement identifies the same consortium and collective 100% ownership, but describes a transaction subject to approvals. Do not use that announcement date as the verified legal closing date.

supporting_sources.supports: Formation, consortium membership, collective ownership and announcement-versus-closing distinction.
APG Infrastructure Pool 2017 II reports an investment in Arevon Energy JV V, LLC, not an expressly identified ownership interest in Arevon Energy, Inc.
The current About page does not resolve investor-vehicle attribution.

contradiction_check: The current About page's omission of shareholders does not establish an ownership exit.
Arevon Energy JV V, LLC cannot be substituted for Arevon Energy, Inc.; the APG disclosure's 6.5% portfolio weighting is not a company ownership percentage.
The sustainability report lists managed energy-asset funds separately from corporate shareholders; those fund names do not establish ownership of Arevon Energy, Inc.
The report states a January–December 2022 reporting period but an August 31, 2022 publication date. Preserve that inconsistency rather than invent a corrected publication date.
outside_release_route: Any new legal shareholder organization, ownership chain, company-identity merge or canonical-name rewrite requires separate handling.
remaining_gap: Exact legal investment vehicles for APG and CalSTRS, the name of ADIA's shareholder subsidiary, individual ownership percentages and current confirmation beyond the historical ownership disclosure. These gaps do not invalidate the supported institutional names.

inaccessible_sources.status: Fetch failed; not used as substantive evidence.
The packet's earlier CalSTRS 404 URL was not supplied, so that exact failed URL could not be retested.

name: FirstEnergy Transmission, LLC
decision: No change to the supported Brookfield Super-Core attribution. Park the ADIA-specific addition because the cited annual-report attachment and footnote could not be independently retrieved.

decision_primary.quotation: Investor’s interest in FET has increased from 19.9% to 49.9%
decision_primary.pdf_page_footnote: HTML Form 8-K, Item 1.01; no PDF page or applicable footnote.

preserved_ownership_facts: North American Transmission Company II L.P. is the identified direct investor and a controlled investment vehicle of Brookfield Super-Core Infrastructure Partners.
The additional 30% acquisition closed March 25, 2024, increasing that investor's interest from 19.9% to 49.9%; FirstEnergy retained 50.1%.

Brookfield Super-Core Infrastructure Partners L.P., its NUS L.P. and its ER SCSp are identified as guarantors. Their appearance does not establish separate direct company stakes or an allocation among parallel funds.

supporting_sources.supports: Completed initial 19.9% transaction.
Case 25-E-0045 exists; the indexed docket identifies a public 2026 annual report for Black Volt B 2024 LLC and Black Beacon B 2024 LLC, filed February 2, 2026.

unverified_packet_evidence.reported_fact: ADIA 10%, described as passive indirect economic exposure on a look-through basis through an intermediate unrelated vehicle.

contradiction_check: If the supplied footnote is accurate, it supports indirect economic exposure, not an additional direct 10% shareholder line.
Do not add the reported ADIA percentage to the 49.9%/50.1% direct ownership split or assign the unnamed intermediate vehicle to a presumed ADIA fund.
January 30 could be the document date and February 2 the filing date; the docket entry alone does not resolve that distinction.
outside_release_route: Creating an ADIA ownership relationship, changing the direct ownership structure or creating the unidentified intermediate organization is outside the permitted attribution-only route.
remaining_gap: The actual annual-report PDF URL; the exact Table 3 row, denominator and footnote 5 wording; and the intermediate vehicle's identity. Brookfield's verified name and existing-fund attribution need not wait for these.

inaccessible_sources.status: Docket shell and indexed filing description accessible; attachment link and PDF content were not exposed through the available retrieval.

name: Sempra Infrastructure Partners, LP
decision: Separate historical KKR fund exposure, the later Fund V commitment, Mubadala's consortium participation, ADIA's holding vehicle and CPP's proposed indirect co-investment. Do not mark the 2025 transaction closed.

supported_changes.exact_change: Support a historical existing-fund link to KKR Global Infrastructure Investors III L.P.; the LP filing identifies Sempra Global, LP, the company's former name.
supported_changes.route: Existing-fund link only; conditional on an existing matching fund record.

application_primary.quotation: Sempra Global, LP US ... KKR Global Infrastructure Investors III L.P.
application_primary.pdf_page_footnote: PDF page 168; packet page 166; monitoring-report page 7 of 15; New Underlying Fund Investments table. No row-specific footnote.
application_primary.source_type: Public pension investment filing; underlying portfolio schedule, not commercial database authority.

supported_changes.exact_change: Support KKR Global Infrastructure Investors V attribution for the later committed investment, explicitly classified as committed/pending rather than completed ownership.
supported_changes.route: Attribution metadata and existing-fund link only.

application_primary.quotation: The Fund has already committed over $9 billion across investments ... Sempra Infrastructure
application_primary.pdf_page_footnote: PDF page 1; investment-list paragraph. Footnote 1 concerns aggregate fundraising, not Sempra ownership.

supported_changes.exact_change: Describe Mubadala as a participant in the 2021 KKR-led consortium, without assigning an independent direct stake or an invented fund.
supported_changes.route: Attribution metadata only; no ownership-structure mutation.

application_primary.quotation: Mubadala invested in Sempra Infrastructure as part of a KKR-led consortium in 2021.

supported_changes.exact_change: Record ADIA's disclosed vehicle as Black Silverback ZC 2022 LP, assignee of Black River B 2017 Inc. Record CPP as a proposed indirect co-investor with KKR, not a separate additive direct shareholder.
supported_changes.route: Attribution notes only; do not create organizations or change ownership relationships.

application_primary.quotation: Black Silverback ZC 2022 LP (assignee of Black River B 2017 Inc.) ... CPPIB will participate as an indirect co-investor with KKR
application_primary.pdf_page_footnote: PDF/printed page 27, ADIA definition; PDF/printed page 24, Slide 4 endnote 7 for CPP.

preserved_ownership_facts: October 1, 2021: the 20% sale closed to KKR Pinnacle Investor L.P., successor-in-interest to KKR Pinnacle Aggregator L.P.; Sempra retained 80%.
By June 1, 2022: the additional 10% ADIA-affiliate sale was completed; the disclosed ownership became Sempra 70%, KKR 20% and ADIA 10%.

September 22, 2025: an agreement was signed for an additional 45% sale to KKR affiliates; announced September 23. The contemplated post-closing split was Sempra 25%, the KKR-led group 65% and ADIA 10%, with CPP participating indirectly within the KKR arrangement.
The latest closing-status source retrieved, dated August 20, 2026, still expected the 45% transaction to close in the third quarter of 2026.

supporting_sources.supports: Completed 20% sale, exact KKR purchaser and Sempra Global identity cross-reference.
Black River B 2017 Inc. was the original ADIA-affiliate purchaser; Infinity Investments S.A. and Azure Vista C 2020 S.à.r.l. were guarantors, not additional disclosed shareholders.
Completed ADIA transaction and 70%/20%/10% ownership disclosure.
Additional 45% transaction and indirect CPP participation; post-closing ownership is conditional.
Sempra Infrastructure transaction remained expected to close in Q3 2026.

contradiction_check: The completed Ecogas sale is not a closing announcement for Sempra Infrastructure Partners.
KKR's Fund V release explicitly lists Sempra Infrastructure among commitments; this is company-specific attribution, not an inference from fundraising alone.
The LP schedule's August 2021 investment-date field does not override the SEC's October 1, 2021 legal closing date.
Mubadala and ADIA are distinct investors with different disclosed participation paths.
A guarantor, acquisition holding vehicle, institutional co-investor and investment fund are not interchangeable.
outside_release_route: Company-name crosswalks, legal-entity creation, shareholder-chain changes, direct-stake updates and recognition of a new closing must be handled separately.
remaining_gap: No closing announcement for the additional 45% transaction was found through September 8, 2026. Exact CPP and Mubadala holding vehicles and completed allocations remain unresolved; do not invent them or treat the full proposed 65% as Fund V's standalone stake.

inaccessible_sources.status: Full article body was not retrievable; Sempra's filing and presentation independently establish proposed indirect participation.

name: Alberta Schools Alternative Procurement I
decision: The supported investment vehicle is International Public Partnerships Limited. Align an existing vehicle link where necessary; do not rewrite equivalent production wording. April 2013 was the remaining-interest acquisition, not initial investment.

supported_changes.exact_change: Align attribution to International Public Partnerships Limited, the listed investment company. Distinguish it from adviser Amber Fund Management Limited and project company BBPP Alberta Schools Limited.
supported_changes.route: Attribution metadata and existing-vehicle link only.

application_primary.quotation: INPP, as the existing owner of 75% of the share capital in BBPP Alberta Schools Limited
application_primary.pdf_page_footnote: HTML issuer RNS 5599B; acquisition paragraphs and Notes to Editors.
application_primary.source_type: Issuer regulatory announcement distributed by RNS and reproduced by Investegate.

preserved_ownership_facts: Scope: 18 schools, comprising nine in Edmonton and nine in Calgary, under ASAP I.
INPP invested from inception; original financial close occurred in September 2008.
The April 4, 2013 announcement confirms acquisition of the remaining 25% from GVest GP Inc., increasing the existing 75% interest to 100%.
The 2024 annual report reports a 100% interest in BBPP Alberta Schools Limited as of December 31, 2024; the current case study also reports 100% equity ownership.

supporting_sources.supports: 18-school scope, 100% equity and September 2008 financial close.

supporting_sources.pdf_page_footnote: PDF page 56, printed page 108; Note 20, Unconsolidated Subsidiaries.
supporting_sources.supports: BBPP Alberta Schools Limited, Canada, 100% ownership.
Express identification of the project as Alberta Schools Alternative Procurement (ASAP I).

contradiction_check: The April 2013 date must not replace September 2008 as initial investment/financial-close history.
Amber's advisory role does not make Amber the equity owner.
The project company, listed investment company and similarly named intermediate subsidiaries are different entities.
outside_release_route: Project-company identity changes, canonical-name rewrites and correction of historical ownership or investment-date fields require separate handling.
remaining_gap: No substantive gap blocks the INPP vehicle alignment. Any intermediate holding-chain reconstruction is additional work, not a prerequisite to the supported name.

name: Conterra Networks
decision: Both Fiera's named funds and a specific APG pool are supported. Preserve the 2019 minority transaction separately from the completed June 30, 2021 change of control.

supported_changes.exact_change: Support Fiera attribution to EICLP and EISCSp; align existing links to EagleCrest Infrastructure Canada LP and EagleCrest Infrastructure SCSp using the regulator's full-name corroboration.
supported_changes.route: Attribution metadata and existing-fund links only.

application_primary.pdf_page_footnote: HTML asset page; Initial Investment, Funds and Status fields.

supported_changes.exact_change: Support historical APG attribution to APG Infrastructure Pool 2020-2021 through Draden Investors, LLC; do not stop at manager-only APG or treat the pool as the direct owner of each operating subsidiary.
supported_changes.route: Attribution metadata and existing-fund link only.

application_primary.quotation: The sole member and owner of all of the economic interest in APG US is APG Infrastructure Pool 2020-2021
application_primary.pdf_page_footnote: PDF/printed page 4, footnotes 31–32; page 3 identifies Draden Investors, LLC. Footnote 32 addresses depositary legal authority.

preserved_ownership_facts: Fiera's current page reports initial investment in 2019 and unrealized status.
The 2019 company announcement explicitly retained Court Square as majority owner, with Fiera a minority investor and management also holding interests.
The June 30, 2021 announcement reports completion of the APG/Fiera acquisition from Court Square affiliates and other indirect holders, with management participation.

A regulator-filed consummation notice independently confirms completion on June 30, 2021. Fiera's controlled side includes co-investment interests; it is not automatically identical to ownership by the two flagship funds.

supporting_sources.supports: Company-issued confirmation of Court Square majority ownership after Fiera's minority investment.
Completed purchase and management participation.
Completed transfer involving EagleCrest CUB GP Inc. and Draden Investors, LLC.
Full names of EagleCrest Infrastructure Canada LP and EagleCrest Infrastructure SCSp.

contradiction_check: Court Square's 2019 majority status is historical, not the post-2021 position.
The FCC document uses both 49.9% and 49.99% for APG in different passages. Do not deploy a precise percentage correction from that internally inconsistent text.
Foreign-ownership approval ceilings and overlapping indirect interests cannot be added together as a company capitalization table.
outside_release_route: Ownership percentages, new acquisition or depositary organizations, shareholder-chain changes and canonical-text rewrites are separate from the permitted fund attribution.
remaining_gap: Current allocations among Fiera funds and co-investors, and any post-2021 APG vehicle changes, were not established. Neither gap blocks the supported named-fund attribution with its historical scope.

inaccessible_sources.status: This version failed; the official DA-21-541A1.pdf version was accessible and used.

name: IonicBlue
decision: Direct company-specific evidence resolves the Fund II attribution.

supported_changes.exact_change: Support an existing-fund link to Apollo Infrastructure Opportunities Fund II LP, abbreviated AIOF II.
supported_changes.route: Attribution metadata and existing-fund link only.

application_primary.quotation: AIOF II has invested ... formed the Ionic Blue joint venture with Johnson Controls
application_primary.pdf_page_footnote: HTML release; paragraph identifying completed AIOF II investments.

preserved_ownership_facts: IonicBlue is the Johnson Controls/Apollo infrastructure joint venture.
The original August 12, 2021 announcement referred generally to funds managed by Apollo affiliates; it did not itself identify Fund II.

supporting_sources.supports: Original joint-venture relationship and generic Apollo-affiliated-funds wording.

contradiction_check: The January 2022 release explicitly places formation of Ionic Blue within the AIOF II investment list. This is not an inference from a fundraise or from an adjacent description of Apollo's infrastructure business.
outside_release_route: No change to company identity, brand spacing, joint-venture organizations or ownership percentages.
remaining_gap: Exact legal holding entities, joint-venture percentages and current allocated capital are not established. These are not prerequisites to the supported historical AIOF II link.

name: US Wind
decision: Direct subsequent evidence establishes AIOF II attribution while preserving the structured-financing distinction.

supported_changes.exact_change: Support an existing-fund link to Apollo Infrastructure Opportunities Fund II LP; do not characterize the entire financing commitment as purchased common equity.
supported_changes.route: Attribution metadata and existing-fund link only.

application_primary.pdf_page_footnote: HTML release; AIOF II investment-list paragraph.

preserved_ownership_facts: Apollo's August 14, 2020 announcement describes a structured investment and commitment of up to $265 million through convertible debt and equity.
The commitment supported acquisition of an equity stake and project development/construction; it does not establish that $265 million was fully funded or entirely equity.
The same announcement identifies Renexia S.p.A. as majority owner and Renexia as a subsidiary of Toto Holding S.p.A.; preserve these as historical disclosures.

supporting_sources.supports: Financing instruments, commitment ceiling and historical Renexia majority ownership.

contradiction_check: The 2020 release's general discussion of Apollo's second infrastructure fund would not alone be decisive. The January 2022 release separately and explicitly identifies US Wind as an AIOF II investment. Neither establishes an Apollo majority stake.
outside_release_route: No company-name rewrite, conversion of debt to equity, ownership-percentage mutation or deletion of Renexia's historically disclosed majority position.
remaining_gap: Current ownership percentages, conversion history, actual funded amounts and exact holding entities remain unresolved; none blocks the historical fund assignment.

name: Lincoln Terminal Holdings

supported_changes.exact_change: Support an existing-fund link to Ara Infrastructure Fund I; preserve the distinction from Ara's private-equity fund series.
supported_changes.route: Attribution metadata and existing-fund link only.

application_primary.quotation: The Fund now owns 12 operational assets ... Portfolio companies include: ... Lincoln
application_primary.pdf_page_footnote: HTML release; named-fund introduction and portfolio-company list.

The current portfolio card identifies Lincoln as an active infrastructure investment, dates investment to November 2022 and explicitly labels the fund Infra Fund I.

supporting_sources.supports: Completed majority acquisition and disclosed legal company name.
Explicit Infra Fund I attribution, active status and November 2022 investment date.

name: MXT Holdings
decision: Support AAIF V label alignment. Subsequent company and sponsor evidence supports an implemented investment, but the sponsor's invested date should not automatically become a legal closing-date field.

supported_changes.exact_change: Align an existing-fund link to Ardian Americas Infrastructure Fund V, corresponding to the source label Ardian Americas Infrastructure Fund (AAIF) V. Do not rewrite already equivalent canonical text.
supported_changes.route: Existing-fund link or attribution alias only.

application_primary.quotation: It is the second transaction from the Ardian Americas Infrastructure Fund (AAIF) V.

preserved_ownership_facts: The July 2023 announcement concerned a signed agreement for 50% co-control alongside Mexico Infrastructure Partners, subject to closing conditions and regulatory approvals.
Ardian's subsequent portfolio entry records MXT as invested on October 30, 2023.
MXT's own subsequent article states that Ardian now controls 50%, supporting implementation rather than leaving the relationship classified solely as an uncompleted announcement.

supporting_sources.supports: Sponsor-reported investment occurrence and investment date.

supporting_sources.quotation: Ardian now controls 50% of MXT Holdings.
supporting_sources.supports: Company confirmation of implemented 50% participation.

contradiction_check: The July 5 announcement date is not the closing date.
The subsequent portfolio and company statements are consistent with the announced 50% transaction having occurred.
The phrase invested on October 30 is not an express legal closing statement.
MXT's loose description of Ardian itself as a fund does not override Ardian's precise AAIF V attribution.
outside_release_route: Exact closing-date updates, capitalization-table changes, new MIP vehicle assignments, company-identity changes and canonical fund-name rewrites require separate handling.
remaining_gap: An express direct-source legal closing notice or filing establishing the closing date and final legal purchaser chain was not retrieved. This does not block AAIF V alignment or recognition of the subsequently confirmed investment.

name: InTransit BC
decision: Correct the BCI evidence's fund, year and ownership scope. Preserve CDPQ's independently documented historical interest without inventing a CDPQ Infrastructure fund.

supported_changes.exact_change: Attribute the cited BCI investment to Bolsena Fund. Annotate 28.7% as the 2021 comparative and 28.4% as the 2022 fund-specific interest, held through intermediary corporations; neither is a current BCI-wide ownership percentage.
supported_changes.route: Attribution metadata and existing-fund link only; ownership-percentage fields require separate handling.

application_primary.quotation: BOLSENA FUND ... InTransit BC Limited Partnership
application_primary.pdf_page_footnote: PDF page 21, printed page 21: 2022 ownership/voting interest 28.4%. PDF page 22, printed page 22: 2021 ownership/voting interest 28.7%. Heading: Involvement with Subsidiaries and Associates. No row-specific footnote; the introductory text establishes intermediary holding corporations.

supported_changes.exact_change: Describe CDPQ Infrastructure as an institutional infrastructure investment program unless a specific legal fund is independently established. Do not create a fund or substitute the separate CDPQ Infra subsidiary.
supported_changes.route: Attribution-type metadata only; no ownership-organization substitution.

application_primary.quotation: Our team makes direct investments in companies involved in various types of infrastructure

preserved_ownership_facts: Bolsena's table classifies InTransit BC Limited Partnership as an associate and the security as a limited partnership interest.

CDPQ's consolidated 2014 annual report independently reports a 33.3% ownership interest in Intransit BC Limited Partnership for both December 31, 2014 and December 31, 2013. This establishes those historical dates, not current ownership or the exact direct holding entity.
CDPQ Infra is a separately identified wholly owned subsidiary; that fact does not establish its ownership of InTransit BC.

supporting_sources.pdf_page_footnote: PDF page 184, printed page 182; Interests in Other Entities, Associates table; Intransit BC Limited Partnership row. No row-specific footnote.
supporting_sources.supports: Historical CDPQ 33.3% ownership interest.
CDPQ Infra is a wholly owned subsidiary, distinct from the institution's infrastructure portfolio/program.

contradiction_check: The BCI document covers multiple pooled funds; its umbrella title is not the name of the fund owning the cited interest.
The packet's 28.7% is a 2021 comparative, not the reported 2022 figure.
Fund-specific indirect exposure and institution-wide ownership are different scopes. No company stake is inferred from portfolio totals.
Historical CDPQ 33.3% and Bolsena's later fund-specific percentages cannot be combined into a single contemporary capitalization table.
outside_release_route: Changing company identity, direct ownership percentages, shareholder structures or organizational records is outside the attribution-only release route.
remaining_gap: Current institution-wide BCI and CDPQ ownership, all intermediate holding entities and any specifically constituted CDPQ fund remain unverified. The Bolsena fund-name correction and historical year/scope annotations are supported.

inaccessible_sources.status: The packet's old TransLink 404 URL was not supplied. It was not used; accessible BCI and CDPQ financial statements provide the decisive evidence.
